records.text: Audio codecs are data compression formats used to encode and decode audio signals. They reduce the amount of data required to represent sound, enabling efficient storage and transmission over networks. Common audio codecs include MP3, AAC, WAV, FLAC, and ALAC. Each codec offers a trade-off between audio quality, file size, and computational complexity. For example, MP3 provides good compression with moderate quality loss, while FLAC offers lossless compression preserving original audio fidelity. Codecs work by removing redundant or less perceptible information from the audio signal, based on human hearing characteristics.
